scenes.line1: How can APIs avoid duplicate POSTs?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how APIs avoid creating duplicate payments when clients retry requests? Let’s break down the key features that keep things reliable.

scenes.label: Idempotency
scenes.sub: Unique keys let servers ignore repeated POSTs.
scenes.say: Idempotency keys are unique values sent with POST requests. They let servers recognize and ignore duplicates, so only one payment gets created even if you retry.

scenes.title: Retries & Rate Limits
scenes.say: When clients retry, APIs should handle it gracefully. Rate limits protect resources, and a status code like four two nine warns clients when they’ve gone over the limit.
Here’s how I design APIs: I use idempotency keys to prevent duplicates, handle retries safely, and always enforce rate limits to protect against abuse.

scenes.question: What happens if you skip idempotency?
scenes.right: Skipping keys risks duplicate resources on retries.
scenes.say: Interview trap: If you skip idempotency keys, clients can accidentally create duplicate resources when they retry. Always include them for non-idempotent operations.
